summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for severe recurrent major depression with psychotic features and suicidal ideation, complicated by chronic pain, opioid dependence, and chronic pancreatitis. She presented with profound hopelessness and a history of self-harm, but engaged in treatment during her stay. Psychiatric medications were optimized with the addition of quetiapine to address psychotic symptoms and improve sleep, while continuing sertraline, mirtazapine, and methadone with therapeutic drug monitoring. A J-tube malfunction was corrected on admission, and radiographic imaging confirmed proper placement in the jejunum. The patient participated in counseling, reported reduced suicidal thoughts, and denied active self-harm ideation by discharge. She was stabilized, educated on medication and J-tube care, and discharged with outpatient follow-up for psychiatry and pain management. Allergies to milk and other foods were documented and addressed in care planning.
